page: Microsoft Azure F64-16amds_v7 is a specialized virtual machine configuration providing a high memory-to-core allocation alongside fast local NVMe storage. Powered by AMD EPYC 9V45 processors clocked up to 4.5 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provisions 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs with 1 thread per core. The platform integrates 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, and includes 7559 GB of bundled NVMe SSD local storage without discrete GPUs. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, as well as hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, achieving 3650.58 in stress-ng single-core tests along with top-tier compression throughput of 41.04 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 17.94 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Multi-core compute and database operations register in the middle tier, with a PassMark CPU score of 44748.77 and Redis throughput reaching 47.37 million SET operations per second. Memory performance remains strong, reflecting 2889.51 in PassMark memory testing, while uncached memory bandwidth sustains 107.44 GB/sec read and 68.39 GB/sec write. In CPU-based language model inference, text generation for a 135M model attains top-tier throughput at 420.88 tokens per second.

The asymmetric configuration of F64-16amds_v7 constrains multithreaded compute scale to 16 cores while offering an expansive 512 GB memory pool and substantial high-speed local disk capacity. This profile provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy or I/O-intensive workloads that do not require massive CPU core counts, eliminating the need to scale to higher-tier, core-dense instances solely to acquire sufficient memory. Best-fit deployments include in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, data pipeline scratch spaces, and analytical applications constrained by memory footprint rather than parallel processing density.
description: Microsoft Azure F64-16amds_v7 is a memory-dense virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated physical cores (16 vCPUs) on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked up to 4.5 GHz. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features an expansive 512.0 GB of memory (32.0 GB per vCPU) and a bundled 7559 GB local NVMe SSD without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results show top-tier single-threaded performance in stress-ng and compression operations, complemented by strong memory evaluation scores and an uncached read bandwidth of 107.44 GB/sec. Multi-core computational metrics and Redis transaction speeds perform within average industry percentiles due to the 16-core ceiling. By decoupling large memory and NVMe capacity from massive vCPU counts, the instance offers cost-efficient resource density for memory-bound applications. The configuration is well matched for in-memory databases, caching tiers, ETL scratch processing, and memory-intensive analytical workloads.
